options.name: annotation
options.description: Add an annotation to the container. The format is key value, multiple times.

options.name: arch
options.description: Set the architecture for the container. Override the architecture, defaults to hosts, of the image to be pulled. For example, arm.

options.name: attach
options.description: Attach to STDIN, STDOUT or STDERR. The default in Podman is false.

options.name: authfile
options.description: Path of the authentication file. Default is ``${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/containers/auth.json`` (Not available for remote commands) You can also override the default path of the authentication file by setting the ``REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE`` environment variable. ``export REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE=path``

options.name: blkio_weight
options.description: Block IO weight (relative weight) accepts a weight value between 10 and 1000

options.name: blkio_weight_device
options.description: Block IO weight (relative device weight, format DEVICE_NAME[:]WEIGHT).

options.name: cap_add
options.description: List of capabilities to add to the container.

options.name: cap_drop
options.description: List of capabilities to drop from the container.

options.name: cgroup_conf
options.description: When running on cgroup v2, specify the cgroup file to write to and its value.

options.name: cgroup_parent
options.description: Path to cgroups under which the cgroup for the container will be created. If the path is not absolute, the path is considered to be relative to the cgroups path of the init process. Cgroups will be created if they do not already exist.

options.name: cgroupns
options.description: Path to cgroups under which the cgroup for the container will be created.

options.name: cgroups
options.description: Determines whether the container will create CGroups. Valid values are enabled and disabled, which the default being enabled. The disabled option will force the container to not create CGroups, and thus conflicts with CGroup options cgroupns and cgroup-parent.

options.name: chrootdirs
options.description: Path to a directory inside the container that is treated as a chroot directory.

options.name: cidfile
options.description: Write the container ID to the file

options.name: cmd_args
options.description: Any additional command options you want to pass to podman command itself, for example C(--log-level=debug) or C(--syslog). This is NOT command to run in container, but rather options for podman itself. For container command please use I(command) option.

options.name: command
options.description: Override command of container. Can be a string or a list.

options.name: conmon_pidfile
options.description: Write the pid of the conmon process to a file. conmon runs in a separate process than Podman, so this is necessary when using systemd to restart Podman containers.

options.name: cpu_period
options.description: Limit the CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) period

options.name: cpu_quota
options.description: Limit the CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) quota

options.name: cpu_rt_period
options.description: Limit the CPU real-time period in microseconds. Limit the container's Real Time CPU usage. This flag tell the kernel to restrict the container's Real Time CPU usage to the period you specify.

options.name: cpu_rt_runtime
options.description: Limit the CPU real-time runtime in microseconds. This flag tells the kernel to limit the amount of time in a given CPU period Real Time tasks may consume.

options.name: cpu_shares
options.description: CPU shares (relative weight)

options.name: cpus
options.description: Number of CPUs. The default is 0.0 which means no limit.

options.name: cpuset_cpus
options.description: CPUs in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1)

options.name: cpuset_mems
options.description: Memory nodes (MEMs) in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1). Only effective on NUMA systems.

options.name: debug
options.description: Return additional information which can be helpful for investigations.

options.name: decryption_key
options.description: The "key-passphrase" to be used for decryption of images. Key can point to keys and/or certificates.

options.name: delete_depend
options.description: Remove selected container and recursively remove all containers that depend on it. Applies to "delete" command.

options.name: delete_time
options.description: Seconds to wait before forcibly stopping the container. Use -1 for infinite wait. Applies to "delete" command.

options.name: delete_volumes
options.description: Remove anonymous volumes associated with the container. This does not include named volumes created with podman volume create, or the --volume option of podman run and podman create.

options.name: detach
options.description: Run container in detach mode

options.name: detach_keys
options.description: Override the key sequence for detaching a container. Format is a single character or ctrl-value

options.name: device
options.description: Add a host device to the container. The format is <device-on-host>[:<device-on-container>][:<permissions>] (e.g. device /dev/sdc:/dev/xvdc:rwm)

options.name: device_cgroup_rule
options.description: Add a rule to the cgroup allowed devices list. The rule is expected to be in the format specified in the Linux kernel documentation admin-guide/cgroup-v1/devices.

options.name: device_read_bps
options.description: Limit read rate (bytes per second) from a device (e.g. device-read-bps /dev/sda:1mb)

options.name: device_read_iops
options.description: Limit read rate (IO per second) from a device (e.g. device-read-iops /dev/sda:1000)

options.name: device_write_bps
options.description: Limit write rate (bytes per second) to a device (e.g. device-write-bps /dev/sda:1mb)

options.name: device_write_iops
options.description: Limit write rate (IO per second) to a device (e.g. device-write-iops /dev/sda:1000)

options.name: dns
options.description: Set custom DNS servers

options.name: dns_option
options.description: Set custom DNS options

options.name: dns_search
options.description: Set custom DNS search domains (Use dns_search with '' if you don't wish to set the search domain)

options.name: entrypoint
options.description: Overwrite the default ENTRYPOINT of the image

options.name: env
options.description: Set environment variables. This option allows you to specify arbitrary environment variables that are available for the process that will be launched inside of the container.

options.name: env_file
options.description: Read in a line delimited file of environment variables. Doesn't support idempotency. If users changes the file with environment variables it's on them to recreate the container. The file must be present on the REMOTE machine where actual podman is running, not on the controller machine where Ansible is executing. If you need to copy the file from controller to remote machine, use the copy or slurp module.

options.name: env_host
options.description: Use all current host environment variables in container. Defaults to false.

options.name: env_merge
options.description: Preprocess default environment variables for the containers

options.name: etc_hosts
options.description: Dict of host-to-IP mappings, where each host name is a key in the dictionary. Each host name will be added to the container's ``/etc/hosts`` file.

options.name: executable
options.description: Path to C(podman) executable if it is not in the C($PATH) on the machine running C(podman)

options.name: expose
options.description: Expose a port, or a range of ports (e.g. expose "3300-3310") to set up port redirection on the host system.

options.name: force_delete
options.description: Force deletion of container when it's being deleted.

options.name: force_restart
options.description: Force restart of container.

options.name: generate_systemd
options.description: Generate systemd unit file for container.

options.name: gidmap
options.description: Run the container in a new user namespace using the supplied mapping.

options.name: gpus
options.description: GPU devices to add to the container.

options.name: group_add
options.description: Add additional groups to run as

options.name: group_entry
options.description: Customize the entry that is written to the /etc/group file within the container when --user is used.

options.name: health_startup_cmd
options.description: Set a startup healthcheck command for a container.

options.name: health_startup_interval
options.description: Set an interval for the startup healthcheck.

options.name: health_startup_retries
options.description: The number of attempts allowed before the startup healthcheck restarts the container. If set to 0, the container is never restarted. The default is 0.

options.name: health_startup_success
options.description: The number of successful runs required before the startup healthcheck succeeds and the regular healthcheck begins. A value of 0 means that any success begins the regular healthcheck. The default is 0.

options.name: health_startup_timeout
options.description: The maximum time a startup healthcheck command has to complete before it is marked as failed.

options.name: healthcheck
options.description: Set or alter a healthcheck command for a container.

options.name: healthcheck_failure_action
options.description: The action to be taken when the container is considered unhealthy. The action must be one of "none", "kill", "restart", or "stop". The default policy is "none".

options.name: healthcheck_interval
options.description: Set an interval for the healthchecks (a value of disable results in no automatic timer setup) (default "30s")

options.name: healthcheck_retries
options.description: The number of retries allowed before a healthcheck is considered to be unhealthy. The default value is 3.

options.name: healthcheck_start_period
options.description: The initialization time needed for a container to bootstrap. The value can be expressed in time format like 2m3s. The default value is 0s

options.name: healthcheck_timeout
options.description: The maximum time allowed to complete the healthcheck before an interval is considered failed. Like start-period, the value can be expressed in a time format such as 1m22s. The default value is 30s

options.name: hooks_dir
options.description: Each .json file in the path configures a hook for Podman containers. For more details on the syntax of the JSON files and the semantics of hook injection, see oci-hooks(5). Can be set multiple times.

options.name: hostname
options.description: Container host name. Sets the container host name that is available inside the container.

options.name: hostuser
options.description: Add a user account to /etc/passwd from the host to the container. The Username or UID must exist on the host system.

options.name: http_proxy
options.description: By default proxy environment variables are passed into the container if set for the podman process. This can be disabled by setting the http_proxy option to false. The environment variables passed in include http_proxy, https_proxy, ftp_proxy, no_proxy, and also the upper case versions of those. Defaults to true

options.name: image
options.description: Repository path (or image name) and tag used to create the container. If an image is not found, the image will be pulled from the registry. If no tag is included, C(latest) will be used. Can also be an image ID. If this is the case, the image is assumed to be available locally.

options.name: image_strict
options.description: Whether to compare images in idempotency by taking into account a full name with registry and namespaces.

options.name: image_volume
options.description: Tells podman how to handle the builtin image volumes. The options are bind, tmpfs, or ignore (default bind)

options.name: init
options.description: Run an init inside the container that forwards signals and reaps processes. The default is false.

options.name: init_ctr
options.description: (Pods only). When using pods, create an init style container, which is run after the infra container is started but before regular pod containers are started.

options.name: init_path
options.description: Path to the container-init binary.

options.name: interactive
options.description: Keep STDIN open even if not attached. The default is false. When set to true, keep stdin open even if not attached. The default is false.

options.name: ip
options.description: Specify a static IP address for the container, for example '10.88.64.128'. Can only be used if no additional CNI networks to join were specified via 'network:', and if the container is not joining another container's network namespace via 'network container:<name|id>'. The address must be within the default CNI network's pool (default 10.88.0.0/16).

options.name: ip6
options.description: Specify a static IPv6 address for the container

options.name: ipc
options.description: Default is to create a private IPC namespace (POSIX SysV IPC) for the container

options.name: kernel_memory
options.description: Kernel memory limit (format <number>[<unit>], where unit = b, k, m or g) Note - idempotency is supported for integers only.

options.name: label
options.description: Add metadata to a container, pass dictionary of label names and values

options.name: label_file
options.description: Read in a line delimited file of labels

options.name: log_driver
options.description: Logging driver. Used to set the log driver for the container. For example log_driver "k8s-file".

options.name: log_level
options.description: Logging level for Podman. Log messages above specified level ("debug"|"info"|"warn"|"error"|"fatal"|"panic") (default "error")

options.name: log_opt
options.description: Logging driver specific options. Used to set the path to the container log file.

options.name: mac_address
options.description: Specify a MAC address for the container, for example '92:d0:c6:0a:29:33'. Don't forget that it must be unique within one Ethernet network.

options.name: memory
options.description: Memory limit (format 10k, where unit = b, k, m or g) Note - idempotency is supported for integers only.

options.name: memory_reservation
options.description: Memory soft limit (format 100m, where unit = b, k, m or g) Note - idempotency is supported for integers only.

options.name: memory_swap
options.description: A limit value equal to memory plus swap. Must be used with the -m (--memory) flag. The swap LIMIT should always be larger than -m (--memory) value. By default, the swap LIMIT will be set to double the value of --memory Note - idempotency is supported for integers only.

options.name: memory_swappiness
options.description: Tune a container's memory swappiness behavior. Accepts an integer between 0 and 100.

options.name: mount
options.description: Attach a filesystem mount to the container. bind or tmpfs For example mount "type=bind,source=/path/on/host,destination=/path/in/container"

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the container

options.name: network
options.description: Set the Network mode for the container. I(bridge) - create a network stack on the default bridge. I(none) - no networking. I(container:<name|id>) - reuse another container's network stack. I(host) - use the podman host network stack. I(<network-name>|<network-id>) - connect to a user-defined network. I(ns:<path>) - path to a network namespace to join. I(slirp4netns) - use slirp4netns to create a user network stack. This is the default for rootless containers.

options.name: network_aliases
options.description: Add network-scoped alias for the container. A container will only have access to aliases on the first network that it joins. This is a limitation that will be removed in a later release.

options.name: no_healthcheck
options.description: Disable any defined healthchecks for container.

options.name: no_hosts
options.description: Do not create /etc/hosts for the container Default is false.

options.name: oom_kill_disable
options.description: Whether to disable OOM Killer for the container or not. Default is false.

options.name: oom_score_adj
options.description: Tune the host's OOM preferences for containers (accepts -1000 to 1000)

options.name: os
options.description: Override the OS, defaults to hosts, of the image to be pulled. For example, windows.

options.name: passwd
options.description: Allow Podman to add entries to /etc/passwd and /etc/group when used in conjunction with the --user option. This is used to override the Podman provided user setup in favor of entrypoint configurations such as libnss-extrausers.

options.name: passwd_entry
options.description: Customize the entry that is written to the /etc/passwd file within the container when --passwd is used.

options.name: personality
options.description: Personality sets the execution domain via Linux personality(2).

options.name: pid
options.description: Set the PID mode for the container

options.name: pid_file
options.description: When the pidfile location is specified, the container process' PID is written to the pidfile.

options.name: pids_limit
options.description: Tune the container's PIDs limit. Set -1 to have unlimited PIDs for the container.

options.name: platform
options.description: Specify the platform for selecting the image.

options.name: pod
options.description: Run container in an existing pod. If you want podman to make the pod for you, prefix the pod name with "new:"

options.name: pod_id_file
options.description: Run container in an existing pod and read the pod's ID from the specified file. When a container is run within a pod which has an infra-container, the infra-container starts first.

options.name: preserve_fd
options.description: Pass down to the process the additional file descriptors specified in the comma separated list.

options.name: preserve_fds
options.description: Pass down to the process N additional file descriptors (in addition to 0, 1, 2). The total FDs are 3\+N.

options.name: privileged
options.description: Give extended privileges to this container. The default is false.

options.name: publish
options.description: Publish a container's port, or range of ports, to the host. Format - ip:hostPort:containerPort | ip::containerPort | hostPort:containerPort | containerPort In case of only containerPort is set, the hostPort will chosen randomly by Podman.

options.name: publish_all
options.description: Publish all exposed ports to random ports on the host interfaces. The default is false.

options.name: pull
options.description: Pull image policy. The default is 'missing'.

options.name: quadlet_dir
options.description: Path to the directory to write quadlet file in. By default, it will be set as C(/etc/containers/systemd/) for root user, C(~/.config/containers/systemd/) for non-root users.

options.name: quadlet_file_mode
options.description: The permissions of the quadlet file. The O(quadlet_file_mode) can be specified as octal numbers or as a symbolic mode (for example, V(u+rwx) or V(u=rw,g=r,o=r)). For octal numbers format, you must either add a leading zero so that Ansible's YAML parser knows it is an octal number (like V(0644) or V(01777)) or quote it (like V('644') or V('1777')) so Ansible receives a string and can do its own conversion from string into number. Giving Ansible a number without following one of these rules will e

options.name: quadlet_filename
options.description: Name of quadlet file to write. By default it takes C(name) value.

options.name: quadlet_options
options.description: Options for the quadlet file. Provide missing in usual container args options as a list of lines to add.

options.name: rdt_class
options.description: Rdt-class sets the class of service (CLOS or COS) for the container to run in. Requires root.

options.name: read_only
options.description: Mount the container's root filesystem as read only. Default is false

options.name: read_only_tmpfs
options.description: If container is running in --read-only mode, then mount a read-write tmpfs on /run, /tmp, and /var/tmp. The default is true

options.name: recreate
options.description: Use with present and started states to force the re-creation of an existing container.

options.name: requires
options.description: Specify one or more requirements. A requirement is a dependency container that will be started before this container. Containers can be specified by name or ID.

options.name: restart_policy
options.description: Restart policy to follow when containers exit. Restart policy will not take effect if a container is stopped via the podman kill or podman stop commands. Valid values are * no - Do not restart containers on exit * on-failure[:max_retries] - Restart containers when they exit with a non-0 exit code, retrying indefinitely or until the optional max_retries count is hit * always - Restart containers when they exit, regardless of status, retrying indefinitely

options.name: restart_time
options.description: Seconds to wait before forcibly stopping the container when restarting. Use -1 for infinite wait. Applies to "restarted" status.

options.name: retry
options.description: Number of times to retry pulling or pushing images between the registry and local storage in case of failure. Default is 3.

options.name: retry_delay
options.description: Duration of delay between retry attempts when pulling or pushing images between the registry and local storage in case of failure.

options.name: rm
options.description: Automatically remove the container when it exits. The default is false.

options.name: rmi
options.description: After exit of the container, remove the image unless another container is using it. Implies --rm on the new container. The default is false.

options.name: rootfs
options.description: If true, the first argument refers to an exploded container on the file system. The default is false.

options.name: sdnotify
options.description: Determines how to use the NOTIFY_SOCKET, as passed with systemd and Type=notify. Can be container, conmon, ignore. For quadlets it can also be healthy to use the built in health checks, see L(documentation,https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html#notify-defaults-to-false) for more details.

options.name: seccomp_policy
options.description: Specify the policy to select the seccomp profile.

options.name: secrets
options.description: Add the named secrets into the container. The format is C(secret[,opt=opt...]), see L(documentation,https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html#secret-secret-opt-opt) for more details.

options.name: security_opt
options.description: Security Options. For example security_opt "seccomp=unconfined"

options.name: shm_size
options.description: Size of /dev/shm. The format is <number><unit>. number must be greater than 0. Unit is optional and can be b (bytes), k (kilobytes), m(megabytes), or g (gigabytes). If you omit the unit, the system uses bytes. If you omit the size entirely, the system uses 64m

options.name: shm_size_systemd
options.description: Size of systemd-specific tmpfs mounts such as /run, /run/lock, /var/log/journal and /tmp.

options.name: sig_proxy
options.description: Proxy signals sent to the podman run command to the container process. SIGCHLD, SIGSTOP, and SIGKILL are not proxied. The default is true.

options.name: state
options.description: I(absent) - A container matching the specified name will be stopped and removed. I(present) - Asserts the existence of a container matching the name and any provided configuration parameters. If no container matches the name, a container will be created. If a container matches the name but the provided configuration does not match, the container will be updated, if it can be. If it cannot be updated, it will be removed and re-created with the requested config. Image version will be taken into ac

options.name: stop_signal
options.description: Signal to stop a container. Default is SIGTERM.

options.name: stop_time
options.description: Seconds to wait before forcibly stopping the container. Use -1 for infinite wait. Applies to "stopped" status.

options.name: stop_timeout
options.description: Timeout (in seconds) to stop a container. Default is 10.

options.name: subgidname
options.description: Run the container in a new user namespace using the map with 'name' in the /etc/subgid file.

options.name: subuidname
options.description: Run the container in a new user namespace using the map with 'name' in the /etc/subuid file.

options.name: sysctl
options.description: Configure namespaced kernel parameters at runtime

options.name: systemd
options.description: Run container in systemd mode. The default is true.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Maximum time (in seconds) a container is allowed to run before conmon sends it the kill signal. By default containers run until they exit or are stopped by "podman stop".

options.name: timezone
options.description: Set timezone in container. This flag takes area-based timezones, GMT time, as well as local, which sets the timezone in the container to match the host machine. See /usr/share/zoneinfo/ for valid timezones. Remote connections use local containers.conf for defaults.

options.name: tls_verify
options.description: Require HTTPS and verify certificates when pulling images.

options.name: tmpfs
options.description: Create a tmpfs mount. For example tmpfs "/tmp" "rw,size=787448k,mode=1777"

options.name: tty
options.description: Allocate a pseudo-TTY. The default is false.

options.name: uidmap
options.description: Run the container in a new user namespace using the supplied mapping.

options.name: ulimit
options.description: Ulimit options

options.name: umask
options.description: Set the umask inside the container. Defaults to 0022. Remote connections use local containers.conf for defaults.

options.name: unsetenv
options.description: Unset default environment variables for the container.

options.name: unsetenv_all
options.description: Unset all default environment variables for the container.

options.name: user
options.description: Sets the username or UID used and optionally the groupname or GID for the specified command.

options.name: userns
options.description: Set the user namespace mode for the container. It defaults to the PODMAN_USERNS environment variable. An empty value means user namespaces are disabled.

options.name: uts
options.description: Set the UTS mode for the container

options.name: variant
options.description: Use VARIANT instead of the default architecture variant of the container image.

options.name: volume
options.description: Create a bind mount. If you specify, volume /HOST-DIR:/CONTAINER-DIR, podman bind mounts /HOST-DIR in the host to /CONTAINER-DIR in the podman container.

options.name: volumes_from
options.description: Mount volumes from the specified container(s).

options.name: workdir
options.description: Working directory inside the container. The default working directory for running binaries within a container is the root directory (/).
